<h1 id="openfec">OpenFEC v1.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This application programming interface (API) allows you to explore the way candidates and committees fund their campaigns. 

 The Federal Election Commission (FEC) API is a RESTful web service supporting full-text and field-specific searches on FEC data. [Bulk downloads](https://www.fec.gov/data/advanced/?tab=bulk-data) are available on the current site. Information is tied to the underlying forms by file ID and image ID. Data is updated nightly. 

 There are a lot of data, and a good place to start is to use search to find interesting candidates and committees. Then, you can use their IDs to find report or line item details with the other endpoints. If you are interested in individual donors, check out contributor information in the `/schedule_a/` endpoints. 

 <b class="body" id="getting_started_head">Getting started with the openFEC API</b><br> 

 If you would like to use the FEC's API programmatically, you can sign up for your own API key using our form. Alternatively, you can still try out our API without an API key by using the web interface and using DEMO_KEY. Note that when you use the openFEC API you are subject to the [Terms of Service](https://github.com/fecgov/FEC/blob/master/TERMS-OF-SERVICE.md) and [Acceptable Use policy](https://github.com/fecgov/FEC/blob/master/ACCEPTABLE-USE-POLICY.md). 

 Signing up for an API key will enable you to place up to 1,000 calls an hour. Each call is limited to 100 results per page. You can email questions, comments or a request to get a key for 7,200 calls an hour (120 calls per minute) to <a href="mailto:APIinfo@fec.gov">APIinfo@fec.gov</a>. You can also ask questions and discuss the data in a community led [group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/fec-data). 

 The model definitions and schema are available at [/swagger](/swagger/). This is useful for making wrappers and exploring the data. 

 A few restrictions limit the way you can use FEC data. For example, you can’t use contributor lists for commercial purposes or to solicit donations. [Learn more here](https://www.fec.gov/updates/sale-or-use-contributor-information/). 

 [Inspect our source code](https://github.com/fecgov/openFEC). We welcome issues and pull requests!

# Authentication

* API Key (ApiKeyHeaderAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Api-Key**, in: header.

* API Key (ApiKeyQueryAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **api_key**, in: query.

* API Key (apiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **api_key**, in: query.

<h1 id="openfec-candidate">candidate</h1>

Candidate endpoints give you access to information about the people running for office. This information is organized by `candidate_id`. If you're unfamiliar with candidate IDs, using `/candidates/search/` will help you locate a particular candidate. 

 Officially, a candidate is an individual seeking nomination for election to a federal office. People become candidates when they (or agents working on their behalf) raise contributions or make expenditures that exceed $5,000. 

 The candidate endpoints primarily use data from FEC registration [Form 1](https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/fecfrm1.pdf) for committee information and [Form 2](https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/fecfrm2.pdf) for candidate information.

## get/candidate/{candidate_id}/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/candidate/string/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /candidate/{candidate_id}/`


This endpoint is useful for finding detailed information about a particular candidate. Use the
`candidate_id` to find the most recent information about that candidate.


<h3 id="getcandidatecandidateid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|office|query|[string]|false|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|candidate_status|query|[string]|false|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Two-year election cycle in which a candidate runs for office.<br>Calculated from Form 2. The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year. This cycle follows<br>the traditional house election cycle and subdivides the presidential<br>and Senate elections into comparable two-year blocks. To retrieve data for<br>the entire four years of a presidential term or six years of a senatorial term,<br>you will need the `election_full` flag.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|state|query|[string]|false|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|
|district|query|[string]|false|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|year|query|string|false|Retrieve records pertaining to a particular election year. The list of election years is based on a candidate filing a statement of candidacy (F2) for that year.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Name (candidate or committee) to search for. Alias for 'q'.|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|federal_funds_flag|query|boolean|false|A boolean the describes if a presidential candidate has accepted federal funds. The flag will be false for House and Senate candidates.|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|has_raised_funds|query|boolean|false|A boolean that describes if a candidate's committee has ever received any receipts for their campaign for this particular office. (Candidates have separate candidate IDs for each office.)|
|election_year|query|[integer(int32)]|false|Year of election|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|incumbent_challenge|query|[string]|false|One-letter code ('I', 'C', 'O') explaining if the candidate is an incumbent, a challenger, or if the seat is open.|
|party|query|[string]|false|Three-letter code for the party affiliated with a candidate or committee. For example, DEM for Democratic Party and REP for Republican Party.|
|candidate_id|path|string|true|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|office|""|
|office|H|
|office|S|
|office|P|
|candidate_status|""|
|candidate_status|C|
|candidate_status|F|
|candidate_status|N|
|candidate_status|P|
|incumbent_challenge|""|
|incumbent_challenge|I|
|incumbent_challenge|C|
|incumbent_challenge|O|

## get/candidate/{candidate_id}/history/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/candidate/string/history/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /candidate/{candidate_id}/history/`


Find out a candidate's characteristics over time. This is particularly useful if the
candidate runs for the same office in different districts or you want to know more about a candidate's
previous races.

This information is organized by `candidate_id`, so it won't help you find a candidate
who ran for different offices over time; candidates get a new ID for each office.


<h3 id="getcandidatecandidateidhistory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|election_full|query|boolean|false|`True` indicates that full election period of a candidate.<br>`False` indicates that two year election cycle.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|candidate_id|path|string|true|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|

## get/candidate/{candidate_id}/totals/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/candidate/string/totals/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /candidate/{candidate_id}/totals/`


This endpoint provides information about a committee's Form 3, Form 3X, or Form 3P financial reports,
which are aggregated by two-year period. We refer to two-year periods as a `cycle`.

The cycle is named after the even-numbered year and includes the year before it. To obtain
totals from 2013 and 2014, you would use 2014. In odd-numbered years, the current cycle
is the next year — for example, in 2015, the current cycle is 2016.

For presidential and Senate candidates, multiple two-year cycles exist between elections.



<h3 id="getcandidatecandidateidtotals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|election_full|query|boolean|false|`True` indicates that full election period of a candidate.<br>`False` indicates that two year election cycle.|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|candidate_id|path|string|true|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|

## get/candidates/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/candidates/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /candidates/`


Fetch basic information about candidates, and use parameters to filter results to the
candidates you're looking for.

Each result reflects a unique FEC candidate ID. That ID is particular to the candidate for a
particular office sought. If a candidate runs for the same office multiple times, the ID
stays the same. If the same person runs for another office — for example, a House
candidate runs for a Senate office — that candidate will get a unique ID for each office.


<h3 id="getcandidates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|office|query|[string]|false|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|candidate_status|query|[string]|false|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Two-year election cycle in which a candidate runs for office.<br>Calculated from Form 2. The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year. This cycle follows<br>the traditional house election cycle and subdivides the presidential<br>and Senate elections into comparable two-year blocks. To retrieve data for<br>the entire four years of a presidential term or six years of a senatorial term,<br>you will need the `election_full` flag.<br>|

## get/candidates/search/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/candidates/search/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /candidates/search/`


Fetch basic information about candidates and their principal committees.

Each result reflects a unique FEC candidate ID. That ID is assigned to the candidate for a
particular office sought. If a candidate runs for the same office over time, that ID
stays the same. If the same person runs for multiple offices — for example, a House
candidate runs for a Senate office — that candidate will get a unique ID for each office.

The candidate endpoints primarily use data from FEC registration
[Form 1](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecfrm1.pdf) for committee information and
[Form 2](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecfrm2.pdf) for candidate information.


<h3 id="getcandidatessearch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|office|query|[string]|false|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|candidate_status|query|[string]|false|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Two-year election cycle in which a candidate runs for office.<br>Calculated from Form 2. The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year. This cycle follows<br>the traditional house election cycle and subdivides the presidential<br>and Senate elections into comparable two-year blocks. To retrieve data for<br>the entire four years of a presidential term or six years of a senatorial term,<br>you will need the `election_full` flag.<br>|
|district|query|[string]|false|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|

<h1 id="openfec-committee">committee</h1>

Committees are entities that spend and raise money in an election. Their characteristics and relationships with candidates can change over time. 

 You might want to use filters or search endpoints to find the committee you're looking for. Then you can use other committee endpoints to explore information about the committee that interests you. 

 Financial information is organized by `committee_id`, so finding the committee you're interested in will lead you to more granular financial information. 

 The committee endpoints include all FEC filers, even if they aren't registered as a committee. 

 Officially, committees include the committees and organizations that file with the FEC. Several different types of organizations file financial reports with the FEC: 

 *Campaign committees authorized by particular candidates to raise and spend funds in their campaigns. Non-party committees (e.g., PACs), some of which may be sponsored by corporations, unions, trade or membership groups, etc. Political party committees at the national, state, and local levels. Groups and individuals making only independent expenditures Corporations, unions, and other organizations making internal communications* 

 The committee endpoints primarily use data from FEC registration Form 1 and Form 2.


filer. Use the `committee_id` to find the most recent information about the committee.

|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>A two year election cycle that the committee was active- (after original registration<br>date but before expiration date in Form 1s) The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year.<br>|

## get/calendar-dates/export/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/calendar-dates/export/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /calendar-dates/export/`


Returns CSV or ICS for downloading directly into calendar applications like Google, Outlook or other applications.

Combines the election and reporting dates with Commission meetings, conferences, outreach, Advisory Opinions, rules, litigation dates and other
events into one calendar.

State filtering now applies to elections, reports and reporting periods.

Presidential pre-primary report due dates are not shown on even years.
Filers generally opt to file monthly rather than submit over 50 pre-primary election
reports. All reporting deadlines are available at /reporting-dates/ for reference.

This is [the sql function](https://github.com/fecgov/openFEC/blob/develop/data/migrations/V40__omnibus_dates.sql)
that creates the calendar.

<h1 id="openfec-financial">financial</h1>

Fetch key information about a committee's Form 3, Form 3X, or Form 3P financial reports. 

 Most committees are required to summarize their financial activity in each filing; those summaries are included in these files. Generally, committees file reports on a quarterly or monthly basis, but some must also submit a report 12 days before primary elections. Therefore, during the primary season, the period covered by this file may be different for different committees. These totals also incorporate any changes made by committees, if any report covering the period is amended. 

 Information is made available on the API as soon as it's processed. Keep in mind, complex paper filings take longer to process. 

 The financial endpoints use data from FEC [form 5](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecfrm5.pdf), for independent expenditors; or the summary and detailed summary pages of the FEC [Form 3](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecfrm3.pdf), for House and Senate committees; [Form 3X](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecfrm3x.pdf), for PACs and parties; and [Form 3P](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecfrm3p.pdf), for presidential committees.

## get/committee/{committee_id}/reports/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/committee/string/reports/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /committee/{committee_id}/reports/`


Each report represents the summary information from Form 3, Form 3X and Form 3P.
These reports have key statistics that illuminate the financial status of a given committee.
Things like cash on hand, debts owed by committee, total receipts, and total disbursements
are especially helpful for understanding a committee's financial dealings.

By default, this endpoint includes both amended and final versions of each report. To restrict
to only the final versions of each report, use `is_amended=false`; to retrieve only reports that
have been amended, use `is_amended=true`.

Several different reporting structures exist, depending on the type of organization that
submits financial information. To see an example of these reporting requirements,
look at the summary and detailed summary pages of Form 3, Form 3X, and Form 3P.

DISCLAIMER: The field labels contained within this resource are subject to change.  We are attempting to succinctly
label these fields while conveying clear meaning to ensure accessibility for all users.

## get/committee/{committee_id}/totals/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/committee/string/totals/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /committee/{committee_id}/totals/`


This endpoint provides information about a committee's Form 3, Form 3X, or Form 3P financial reports,
which are aggregated by two-year period. We refer to two-year periods as a `cycle`.

The cycle is named after the even-numbered year and includes the year before it. To obtain
totals from 2013 and 2014, you would use 2014. In odd-numbered years, the current cycle
is the next year — for example, in 2015, the current cycle is 2016.

For presidential and Senate candidates, multiple two-year cycles exist between elections.



<h3 id="getcommitteecommitteeidtotals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|committee_id|path|string|true|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|

## get/elections/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/elections/?office=house&cycle=0&api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /elections/`


Look at the top-level financial information for all candidates running for the same
office.

Choose a 2-year cycle, and `house`, `senate` or `presidential`.

If you are looking for a Senate seat, you will need to select the state using a two-letter
abbreviation.

House races require state and a two-digit district number.

Since this endpoint reflects financial information, it will only have candidates once they file
financial reporting forms. Query the `/candidates` endpoint to retrieve an-up-to-date list of all the
candidates that filed to run for a particular seat.


<h3 id="getelections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|office|query|string|true|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|district|query|string|false|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|state|query|string|false|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|
|cycle|query|integer(int32)|true|<br>Two-year election cycle in which a candidate runs for office.<br>Calculated from Form 2. The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year. This cycle follows<br>the traditional house election cycle and subdivides the presidential<br>and Senate elections into comparable two-year blocks. To retrieve data for<br>the entire four years of a presidential term or six years of a senatorial term,<br>you will need the `election_full` flag.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|election_full|query|boolean|false|`True` indicates that full election period of a candidate.<br>`False` indicates that two year election cycle.|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|

## get/reports/{entity_type}/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/reports/presidential/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /reports/{entity_type}/`


Each report represents the summary information from Form 3, Form 3X and Form 3P.
These reports have key statistics that illuminate the financial status of a given committee.
Things like cash on hand, debts owed by committee, total receipts, and total disbursements
are especially helpful for understanding a committee's financial dealings.

By default, this endpoint includes both amended and final versions of each report. To restrict
to only the final versions of each report, use `is_amended=false`; to retrieve only reports that
have been amended, use `is_amended=true`.

Several different reporting structures exist, depending on the type of organization that
submits financial information. To see an example of these reporting requirements,
look at the summary and detailed summary pages of Form 3, Form 3X, and Form 3P.

DISCLAIMER: The field labels contained within this resource are subject to change.  We are attempting to succinctly
label these fields while conveying clear meaning to ensure accessibility for all users.


<h3 id="getreportsentitytype-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|min_debts_owed_amount|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts greater than a value.<br>|
|max_debts_owed_expenditures|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts less than a value.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|year|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Forms with coverage date - <br>    year from the coverage ending date.<br>Forms without coverage date - <br>    year from the receipt date.<br>|
|max_cash_on_hand_end_period_amount|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts less than a value.<br>|
|filer_type|query|string|false|The method used to file with the FEC, either electronic or on paper.|
|max_party_coordinated_expenditures|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts less than a value.<br>|

|max_receipt_date|query|string(date)|false|<br>Selects all items received by FEC before this date(MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD)<br>|

|min_party_coordinated_expenditures|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts greater than a value.<br>|
|committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|min_total_contributions|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts greater than a value.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|

|min_receipt_date|query|string(date)|false|<br>Selects all items received by FEC after this date(MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD)<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|min_independent_expenditures|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts greater than a value.<br>|
|q_filer|query|[string]|false|<br>Keyword search for filer name or ID<br>|
|max_disbursements_amount|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts less than a value.<br>|
|max_total_contributions|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts less than a value.<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|amendment_indicator|query|[string]|false|Amendent types:<br>    -N   new<br>    -A   amendment<br>    -T   terminated<br>    -C   consolidated<br>    -M   multi-candidate<br>    -S   secondary<br><br>NULL might be new or amendment. If amendment indicator is null and the filings is the first or first in a chain treat it as if it was a new. If it is not the first or first in a chain then treat the filing as an amendment.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|

|report_type|query|[string]|false|Report type; prefix with "-" to exclude. Name of report where the underlying data comes from:<br>    - 10D Pre-Election<br>    - 10G Pre-General<br>    - 10P Pre-Primary<br>    - 10R Pre-Run-Off<br>    - 10S Pre-Special<br>    - 12C Pre-Convention<br>    - 12G Pre-General<br>    - 12P Pre-Primary<br>    - 12R Pre-Run-Off<br>    - 12S Pre-Special<br>    - 30D Post-Election<br>    - 30G Post-General<br>    - 30P Post-Primary<br>    - 30R Post-Run-Off<br>    - 30S Post-Special<br>    - 60D Post-Convention<br>    - M1  January Monthly<br>    - M10 October Monthly<br>    - M11 November Monthly<br>    - M12 December Monthly<br>    - M2  February Monthly<br>    - M3  March Monthly<br>    - M4  April Monthly<br>    - M5  May Monthly<br>    - M6  June Monthly<br>    - M7  July Monthly<br>    - M8  August Monthly<br>    - M9  September Monthly<br>    - MY  Mid-Year Report<br>    - Q1  April Quarterly<br>    - Q2  July Quarterly<br>    - Q3  October Quarterly<br>    - TER Termination Report<br>    - YE  Year-End<br>    - ADJ COMP ADJUST AMEND<br>    - CA  COMPREHENSIVE AMEND<br>|
|most_recent|query|boolean|false|<br>Report is either new or is the most-recently filed amendment<br>|
|entity_type|path|string|true|Committee groupings based on FEC filing form.                 Choose one of: `presidential`, `pac-party`, `house-senate`, or `ie-only`|

## get/totals/by_entity/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/totals/by_entity/?cycle=0&api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /totals/by_entity/`


Provides cumulative receipt totals by entity type, over a two year cycle. Totals are adjusted to avoid double counting.

This is [the sql](https://github.com/fecgov/openFEC/blob/develop/data/migrations/V41__large_aggregates.sql) that creates these calculations.


<h3 id="gettotalsbyentity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## get/totals/{entity_type}/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/totals/presidential/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /totals/{entity_type}/`


This endpoint provides information about a committee's Form 3, Form 3X, or Form 3P financial reports,
which are aggregated by two-year period. We refer to two-year periods as a `cycle`.

The cycle is named after the even-numbered year and includes the year before it. To obtain
totals from 2013 and 2014, you would use 2014. In odd-numbered years, the current cycle
is the next year — for example, in 2015, the current cycle is 2016.

For presidential and Senate candidates, multiple two-year cycles exist between elections.

|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|filing_frequency|query|[string]|false|The one-letter <br>    code of the filing frequency:<br>         - A Administratively terminated<br>         - D Debt<br>         - M Monthly filer<br>         - Q Quarterly filer<br>         - T Terminated<br>         - W Waived<br>|
|max_receipts|query|string|false|<br>Filter for all amounts less than a value.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|

|committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|

<h1 id="openfec-filings">filings</h1>

All official records and reports filed by or delivered to the FEC. 

 Note: because the filings data includes many records, counts for large result sets are approximate; you will want to page through the records until no records are returned.

## get/candidate/{candidate_id}/filings/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/candidate/string/filings/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /candidate/{candidate_id}/filings/`


All official records and reports filed by or delivered to the FEC.

Note: because the filings data includes many records, counts for large
result sets are approximate; you will want to page through the records until no records are returned.


<h3 id="getcandidatecandidateidfilings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|office|query|[string]|false|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|file_number|query|[integer(int32)]|false|Filing ID number|
|form_category|query|[string]|false|<br>The forms filed are categorized based on the nature of the filing:<br>    - REPORT F3, F3X, F3P, F3L, F4, F5, F7, F13<br>    - NOTICE F5, F24, F6, F9, F10, F11<br>    - STATEMENT F1, F2<br>    - OTHER F1M, F8, F99, F12, FRQ<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|district|query|[string]|false|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|document_type|query|[string]|false|<br>The type of document for documents other than reports:<br>    - 2 24 Hour Contribution Notice<br>    - 4 48 Hour Contribution Notice<br>    - A Debt Settlement Statement<br>    - B Acknowledgment of Receipt of Debt Settlement Statement<br>    - C RFAI: Debt Settlement First Notice<br>    - D Commission Debt Settlement Review<br>    - E Commission Response TO Debt Settlement Request<br>    - F Administrative Termination<br>    - G Debt Settlement Plan Amendment<br>    - H Disavowal Notice<br>    - I Disavowal Response<br>    - J Conduit Report<br>    - K Termination Approval<br>    - L Repeat Non-Filer Notice<br>    - M Filing Frequency Change Notice<br>    - N Paper Amendment to Electronic Report<br>    - O Acknowledgment of Filing Frequency Change<br>    - S RFAI: Debt Settlement Second<br>    - T Miscellaneous Report TO FEC<br>    - V Repeat Violation Notice (441A OR 441B)<br>    - P Notice of Paper Filing<br>    - R F3L Filing Frequency Change Notice<br>    - Q Acknowledgment of F3L Filing Frequency Change<br>    - U Unregistered Committee Notice<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|state|query|[string]|false|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|
|amendment_indicator|query|[string]|false|Amendent types:<br>    -N   new<br>    -A   amendment<br>    -T   terminated<br>    -C   consolidated<br>    -M   multi-candidate<br>    -S   secondary<br><br>NULL might be new or amendment. If amendment indicator is null and the filings is the first or first in a chain treat it as if it was a new. If it is not the first or first in a chain then treat the filing as an amendment.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|is_amended|query|boolean|false|<br>False indicates that a report is the most recent. True indicates that the report has been superseded by an amendment.<br>|
|filer_type|query|string|false|The method used to file with the FEC, either electronic or on paper.|
|max_receipt_date|query|string(date)|false|<br>Selects all filings received before this date(MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD)<br>|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|primary_general_indicator|query|[string]|false|<br>Primary, general or special election indicator.<br>|
|request_type|query|[string]|false|Requests for additional information (RFAIs) sent to filers. The request type is based on the type of document filed:<br>    - 1 Statement of Organization<br>    - 2 Report of Receipts and Expenditures (Form 3 and 3X)<br>    - 3 Second Notice - Reports<br>    - 4 Request for Additional Information<br>    - 5 Informational - Reports<br>    - 6 Second Notice - Statement of Organization<br>    - 7 Failure to File<br>    - 8 From Public Disclosure<br>    - 9 From Multi Candidate Status<br>|
|report_year|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Forms with coverage date - <br>    year from the coverage ending date.<br>Forms without coverage date - <br>    year from the receipt date.<br>|
|form_type|query|[string]|false|The form where the underlying data comes from, for example, Form 1 would appear as F1:<br>    - F1   Statement of Organization<br>    - F1M  Notification of Multicandidate Status<br>    - F2   Statement of Candidacy<br>    - F3   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee<br>    - F3P  Report of Receipts and Disbursements by an Authorized Committee of a Candidate for     The Office of President or Vice President<br>    - F3L  Report of Contributions Bundled by Lobbyists/Registrants and Lobbyist/Registrant PACs<br>    - F3X  Report of Receipts and Disbursements for other than an Authorized Committee<br>    - F4   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for a Committee or Organization Supporting a Nomination Convention<br>    - F5   Report of Independent Expenditures Made and Contributions Received<br>    - F6   48 Hour Notice of Contributions/Loans Received<br>    - F7   Report of Communication Costs by Corporations and Membership Organizations<br>    - F8   Debt Settlement Plan<br>    - F9   24 Hour Notice of Disbursements for Electioneering Communications<br>    - F13  Report of Donations Accepted for Inaugural Committee<br>    - F99  Miscellaneous Text<br>    - FRQ  Request for Additional Information<br>|
|committee_type|query|string|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|beginning_image_number|query|[string]|false|<br>Unique identifier for the electronic or paper report. This number is used to construct<br>PDF URLs to the original document.<br>|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|sort|query|[string]|false|<br>Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order. ex: `-case_no`<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|min_receipt_date|query|string(date)|false|<br>Selects all filings received after this date(MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD)<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|q_filer|query|[string]|false|<br>Keyword search for filer name or ID<br>|
|report_type|query|[string]|false|Name of report where the underlying data comes from:<br>    - 10D Pre-Election<br>    - 10G Pre-General<br>    - 10P Pre-Primary<br>    - 10R Pre-Run-Off<br>    - 10S Pre-Special<br>    - 12C Pre-Convention<br>    - 12G Pre-General<br>    - 12P Pre-Primary<br>    - 12R Pre-Run-Off<br>    - 12S Pre-Special<br>    - 30D Post-Election<br>    - 30G Post-General<br>    - 30P Post-Primary<br>    - 30R Post-Run-Off<br>    - 30S Post-Special<br>    - 60D Post-Convention<br>    - M1  January Monthly<br>    - M10 October Monthly<br>    - M11 November Monthly<br>    - M12 December Monthly<br>    - M2  February Monthly<br>    - M3  March Monthly<br>    - M4  April Monthly<br>    - M5  May Monthly<br>    - M6  June Monthly<br>    - M7  July Monthly<br>    - M8  August Monthly<br>    - M9  September Monthly<br>    - MY  Mid-Year Report<br>    - Q1  April Quarterly<br>    - Q2  July Quarterly<br>    - Q3  October Quarterly<br>    - TER Termination Report<br>    - YE  Year-End<br>    - ADJ COMP ADJUST AMEND<br>    - CA  COMPREHENSIVE AMEND<br>    - 90S Post Inaugural Supplement<br>    - 90D Post Inaugural<br>    - 48  48 Hour Notification<br>    - 24  24 Hour Notification<br>    - M7S July Monthly/Semi-Annual<br>    - MSA Monthly Semi-Annual (MY)<br>    - MYS Monthly Year End/Semi-Annual<br>    - Q2S July Quarterly/Semi-Annual<br>    - QSA Quarterly Semi-Annual (MY)<br>    - QYS Quarterly Year End/Semi-Annual<br>    - QYE Quarterly Semi-Annual (YE)<br>    - QMS Quarterly Mid-Year/ Semi-Annual<br>    - MSY Monthly Semi-Annual (YE)<br>|

`GET /committee/{committee_id}/filings/`


All official records and reports filed by or delivered to the FEC.

Note: because the filings data includes many records, counts for large
result sets are approximate; you will want to page through the records until no records are returned.

## get/operations-log/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/operations-log/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /operations-log/`


The Operations log contains details of each report loaded into the database. It is primarily
used as status check to determine when all of the data processes, from initial entry through
review are complete.

<h1 id="openfec-receipts">receipts</h1>

This collection of endpoints includes Schedule A records reported by a committee. Schedule A records describe itemized receipts, including contributions from individuals. If you are interested in contributions from individuals, use the /schedules/schedule_a/ endpoint. For a more complete description of all Schedule A records visit [About receipts data](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/about-receipts-data/). If you are interested in our "is_individual" methodology visit our [methodology page](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/methodology/). 

 

 

 Schedule A is also available as a database dump file that is updated weekly on Sunday. The database dump files are here: https://www.fec.gov/files/bulk-downloads/index.html?prefix=bulk-downloads/data-dump/schedules/. The instructions are here: https://www.fec.gov/files//bulk-downloads/data-dump/schedules/README.txt. We cannot provide help with restoring the database dump files, but you can refer to this community led [group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/fec-data) for discussion.

## get/schedules/schedule_a/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_a/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_a/`


This description is for both ​`/schedules​/schedule_a​/` and ​ `/schedules​/schedule_a​/{sub_id}​/`.

This endpoint provides itemized receipts. Schedule A records describe itemized receipts, including contributions from individuals. If you are interested in contributions from an individual, use the `/schedules/schedule_a/` endpoint. For a more complete description of all Schedule A records visit [About receipts data](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/about-receipts-data/). If you are interested in our "is_individual" methodology visit our [methodology page](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/methodology/).

​The `/schedules​/schedule_a​/` endpoint is not paginated by page number. This endpoint uses keyset pagination to improve query performance and these indices are required to properly page through this large dataset. To request the next page, you should append the values found in the `last_indexes` object from pagination to the URL of your last request as additional parameters. 
For example, when sorting by `contribution_receipt_date`, you might receive a page of results with the two scenarios of following pagination information:

case #1:
```
pagination: {
    pages: 2152643,
    per_page: 20,
    count: 43052850,
    last_indexes: {
        last_index: "230880619",
        last_contribution_receipt_date: "2014-01-01"
    }
}
```
<br/>
case #2 (results which include contribution_receipt_date = NULL):

```
pagination: {
    pages: 2152644,
    per_page: 20,
    count: 43052850,
    last_indexes: {
        last_index: "230880639",
        sort_null_only: True
    }
}
```
To fetch the next page of sorted results, append `last_index=230880619` and `last_contribution_receipt_date=2014-01-01` to the URL and when reaching `contribution_receipt_date=NULL`, append `last_index=230880639` and `sort_null_only=True`. We strongly advise paging through these results using sort indices. The default sort is acending by `contribution_receipt_date` (`deprecated`, will be descending). If you do not page using sort indices, some transactions may be unintentionally filtered out.

Calls to ​`/schedules​/schedule_a​/` may return many records. For large result sets, the record counts found in the pagination object are approximate; you will need to page through the records until no records are returned.

To avoid throwing the "out of range" exception on the last page, one recommandation is to use total count and `per_page` to control the traverse loop of results.

​The `/schedules​/schedule_a​/{sub_id}​/` endpoint returns a single transaction, but it does include a pagination object class. Please ignore the information in that object class.



<h3 id="getschedulesschedulea-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_load_date|query|string(date)|false|Maximum load date|
|max_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts less than a value.|
|max_image_number|query|string|false|Maxium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|contributor_occupation|query|[string]|false|Occupation of contributor, filers need to make an effort to gather this information|
|recipient_committee_designation|query|[string]|false|The one-letter designation code of the organization:<br>         - A authorized by a candidate<br>         - J joint fundraising committee<br>         - P principal campaign committee of a candidate<br>         - U unauthorized<br>         - B lobbyist/registrant PAC<br>         - D leadership PAC<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|is_individual|query|boolean|false|Restrict to non-earmarked individual contributions where memo code is true. Filtering individuals is useful to make sure contributions are not double reported and in creating breakdowns of the amount of money coming from individuals.|
|line_number|query|string|false|Filter for form and line number using the following format: `FORM-LINENUMBER`.  For example an argument such as `F3X-16` would filter down to all entries from form `F3X` line number `16`.|
|contributor_type|query|[string]|false|Filters individual or committee contributions based on line number|
|recipient_committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|contributor_zip|query|[string]|false|Zip code of contributor|
|contributor_city|query|[string]|false|City of contributor|
|last_index|query|integer(int32)|false|Index of last result from previous page|
|last_contribution_receipt_amount|query|number(float)|false|When sorting by `contribution_receipt_amount`, this is populated with the         `contribution_receipt_amount` of the last result. However, you will need to pass the index         of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|contributor_id|query|[string]|false|The FEC identifier should be represented here if the contributor is registered with the FEC.|
|recipient_committee_org_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter code for the kind for organization:<br>        - C corporation<br>        - L labor organization<br>        - M membership organization<br>        - T trade association<br>        - V cooperative<br>        - W corporation without capital stock<br>|
|contributor_state|query|[string]|false|State of contributor|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|two_year_transaction_period|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>This is a two-year period that is derived from the year a transaction took place in the<br>Itemized Schedule A and Schedule B tables. In cases where we have the date of the transaction<br>(contribution_receipt_date in schedules/schedule_a, disbursement_date in schedules/schedule_b)<br>the two_year_transaction_period is named after the ending, even-numbered year. If we do not<br>have the date  of the transaction, we fall back to using the report year (report_year in both<br>tables) instead,  making the same cycle adjustment as necessary. If no transaction year is<br>specified, the results default to the most current cycle.<br>|
|min_date|query|string(date)|false|Minimum date|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|contributor_employer|query|[string]|false|Employer of contributor, filers need to make an effort to gather this information|
|min_load_date|query|string(date)|false|Minimum load date|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|last_contribution_receipt_date|query|string(date)|false|When sorting by `contribution_receipt_date`, this is populated with the         `contribution_receipt_date` of the last result. However, you will need to pass the index         of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|min_image_number|query|string|false|Minium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|contributor_name|query|[string]|false|Name of contributor|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|image_number|query|[string]|false|<br>An unique identifier for each page where the electronic or paper filing is reported.<br>|
|min_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts greater than a value.|
|max_date|query|string(date)|false|Maximum date|

## get/schedules/schedule_a/by_employer/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_a/by_employer/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_a/by_employer/`


This endpoint provides itemized individual contributions received by a committee, aggregated by the contributor’s employer name. If you are interested in our “is_individual” methodology, review the [methodology page](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/methodology). Unitemized individual contributions are not included.


<h3 id="getschedulesscheduleabyemployer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|employer|query|[string]|false|Employer of contributor as reported on the committee's filing|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "pagination": {
    "count": 0,
    "page": 0,
    "pages": 0,
    "per_page": 0
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "committee_id": "string",
      "count": 0,
      "cycle": 0,
      "employer": "string",
      "total": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

## get/schedules/schedule_a/by_size/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_a/by_size/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_a/by_size/`


This endpoint provides individual contributions received by a committee, aggregated by size:

```
 - $200 and under
 - $200.01 - $499.99
 - $500 - $999.99
 - $1000 - $1999.99
 - $2000 +
```

The $200.00 and under category includes contributions of $200 or less combined with unitemized individual contributions.


<h3 id="getschedulesscheduleabysize-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|size|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>The total all contributions in the following ranges:<br>```<br>  -0    $200 and under<br>  -200  $200.01 - $499.99<br>  -500  $500 - $999.99<br>  -1000 $1000 - $1999.99<br>  -2000 $2000 +<br>```<br>Unitemized contributions are included in the `0` category.<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|size|0|
|size|200|
|size|500|
|size|1000|
|size|2000|

```json
    "count": 0,
    "page": 0,
    "pages": 0,
    "per_page": 0
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "committee_id": "string",
      "count": 0,
      "cycle": 0,
      "size": 0,
      "total": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_a/efile/`

## get/schedules/schedule_a/{sub_id}/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_a/string/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_a/{sub_id}/`


This description is for both ​`/schedules​/schedule_a​/` and ​ `/schedules​/schedule_a​/{sub_id}​/`.

This endpoint provides itemized receipts. Schedule A records describe itemized receipts, including contributions from individuals. If you are interested in contributions from an individual, use the `/schedules/schedule_a/` endpoint. For a more complete description of all Schedule A records visit [About receipts data](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/about-receipts-data/). If you are interested in our "is_individual" methodology visit our [methodology page](https://www.fec.gov/campaign-finance-data/about-campaign-finance-data/methodology/).

​The `/schedules​/schedule_a​/` endpoint is not paginated by page number. This endpoint uses keyset pagination to improve query performance and these indices are required to properly page through this large dataset. To request the next page, you should append the values found in the `last_indexes` object from pagination to the URL of your last request as additional parameters. 
For example, when sorting by `contribution_receipt_date`, you might receive a page of results with the two scenarios of following pagination information:

case #1:
```
pagination: {
    pages: 2152643,
    per_page: 20,
    count: 43052850,
    last_indexes: {
        last_index: "230880619",
        last_contribution_receipt_date: "2014-01-01"
    }
}
```
<br/>
case #2 (results which include contribution_receipt_date = NULL):

```
pagination: {
    pages: 2152644,
    per_page: 20,
    count: 43052850,
    last_indexes: {
        last_index: "230880639",
        sort_null_only: True
    }
}
```
To fetch the next page of sorted results, append `last_index=230880619` and `last_contribution_receipt_date=2014-01-01` to the URL and when reaching `contribution_receipt_date=NULL`, append `last_index=230880639` and `sort_null_only=True`. We strongly advise paging through these results using sort indices. The default sort is acending by `contribution_receipt_date` (`deprecated`, will be descending). If you do not page using sort indices, some transactions may be unintentionally filtered out.

Calls to ​`/schedules​/schedule_a​/` may return many records. For large result sets, the record counts found in the pagination object are approximate; you will need to page through the records until no records are returned.

To avoid throwing the "out of range" exception on the last page, one recommandation is to use total count and `per_page` to control the traverse loop of results.

​The `/schedules​/schedule_a​/{sub_id}​/` endpoint returns a single transaction, but it does include a pagination object class. Please ignore the information in that object class.



<h3 id="getschedulesscheduleasubid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_load_date|query|string(date)|false|Maximum load date|
|max_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts less than a value.|
|max_image_number|query|string|false|Maxium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|contributor_occupation|query|[string]|false|Occupation of contributor, filers need to make an effort to gather this information|
|recipient_committee_designation|query|[string]|false|The one-letter designation code of the organization:<br>         - A authorized by a candidate<br>         - J joint fundraising committee<br>         - P principal campaign committee of a candidate<br>         - U unauthorized<br>         - B lobbyist/registrant PAC<br>         - D leadership PAC<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|is_individual|query|boolean|false|Restrict to non-earmarked individual contributions where memo code is true. Filtering individuals is useful to make sure contributions are not double reported and in creating breakdowns of the amount of money coming from individuals.|
|line_number|query|string|false|Filter for form and line number using the following format: `FORM-LINENUMBER`.  For example an argument such as `F3X-16` would filter down to all entries from form `F3X` line number `16`.|
|contributor_type|query|[string]|false|Filters individual or committee contributions based on line number|
|recipient_committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|contributor_zip|query|[string]|false|Zip code of contributor|
|contributor_city|query|[string]|false|City of contributor|
|last_index|query|integer(int32)|false|Index of last result from previous page|
|last_contribution_receipt_amount|query|number(float)|false|When sorting by `contribution_receipt_amount`, this is populated with the         `contribution_receipt_amount` of the last result. However, you will need to pass the index         of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|contributor_id|query|[string]|false|The FEC identifier should be represented here if the contributor is registered with the FEC.|
|recipient_committee_org_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter code for the kind for organization:<br>        - C corporation<br>        - L labor organization<br>        - M membership organization<br>        - T trade association<br>        - V cooperative<br>        - W corporation without capital stock<br>|
|contributor_state|query|[string]|false|State of contributor|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|two_year_transaction_period|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>This is a two-year period that is derived from the year a transaction took place in the<br>Itemized Schedule A and Schedule B tables. In cases where we have the date of the transaction<br>(contribution_receipt_date in schedules/schedule_a, disbursement_date in schedules/schedule_b)<br>the two_year_transaction_period is named after the ending, even-numbered year. If we do not<br>have the date  of the transaction, we fall back to using the report year (report_year in both<br>tables) instead,  making the same cycle adjustment as necessary. If no transaction year is<br>specified, the results default to the most current cycle.<br>|
|min_date|query|string(date)|false|Minimum date|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|contributor_employer|query|[string]|false|Employer of contributor, filers need to make an effort to gather this information|
|min_load_date|query|string(date)|false|Minimum load date|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|last_contribution_receipt_date|query|string(date)|false|When sorting by `contribution_receipt_date`, this is populated with the         `contribution_receipt_date` of the last result. However, you will need to pass the index         of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|min_image_number|query|string|false|Minium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|contributor_name|query|[string]|false|Name of contributor|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|image_number|query|[string]|false|<br>An unique identifier for each page where the electronic or paper filing is reported.<br>|
|min_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts greater than a value.|
|max_date|query|string(date)|false|Maximum date|
|sub_id|path|string|true|none|

<h1 id="openfec-disbursements">disbursements</h1>

Schedule B filings describe itemized disbursements. This data explains how committees and other filers spend their money. These figures are reported as part of forms F3, F3X and F3P.

## get/schedules/schedule_b/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_b/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_b/`


Schedule B filings describe itemized disbursements. This data
explains how committees and other filers spend their money. These figures are
reported as part of forms F3, F3X and F3P.

The data is divided in two-year periods, called `two_year_transaction_period`, which
is derived from the `report_year` submitted of the corresponding form. If no value is supplied, the results will
default to the most recent two-year period that is named after the ending,
even-numbered year.

Due to the large quantity of Schedule B filings, this endpoint is not paginated by
page number. Instead, you can request the next page of results by adding the values in
the `last_indexes` object from `pagination` to the URL of your last request. For
example, when sorting by `disbursement_date`, you might receive a page of
results with the following pagination information:

```
pagination: {
    pages: 965191,
    per_page: 20,
    count: 19303814,
    last_indexes: {
        last_index: "230906248",
        last_disbursement_date: "2014-07-04"
    }
}
```

To fetch the next page of sorted results, append `last_index=230906248` and
`last_disbursement_date=2014-07-04` to the URL.  We strongly advise paging through
these results by using the sort indices (defaults to sort by disbursement date, e.g.
`last_disbursement_date`), otherwise some resources may be unintentionally filtered out.
This resource uses keyset pagination to improve query performance
and these indices are required to properly page through this large dataset.

Note: because the Schedule B data includes many records, counts for
large result sets are approximate; you will want to page through the records until no records are returned.


<h3 id="getschedulesscheduleb-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disbursement_description|query|[string]|false|Description of disbursement|
|max_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts less than a value.|
|max_image_number|query|string|false|Maxium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|image_number|query|[string]|false|<br>An unique identifier for each page where the electronic or paper filing is reported.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|last_disbursement_date|query|string(date)|false|When sorting by `disbursement_date`, this is populated with the `disbursement_date` of the last result. However, you will need to pass the index of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|line_number|query|string|false|Filter for form and line number using the following format: `FORM-LINENUMBER`.  For example an argument such as `F3X-16` would filter down to all entries from form `F3X` line number `16`.|
|spender_committee_designation|query|[string]|false|The one-letter designation code of the organization:<br>         - A authorized by a candidate<br>         - J joint fundraising committee<br>         - P principal campaign committee of a candidate<br>         - U unauthorized<br>         - B lobbyist/registrant PAC<br>         - D leadership PAC<br>|
|last_disbursement_amount|query|number(float)|false|When sorting by `disbursement_amount`, this is populated with the `disbursement_amount` of the last result.  However, you will need to pass the index of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|last_index|query|integer(int32)|false|Index of last result from previous page|
|spender_committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|two_year_transaction_period|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>This is a two-year period that is derived from the year a transaction took place in the<br>Itemized Schedule A and Schedule B tables. In cases where we have the date of the transaction<br>(contribution_receipt_date in schedules/schedule_a, disbursement_date in schedules/schedule_b)<br>the two_year_transaction_period is named after the ending, even-numbered year. If we do not<br>have the date  of the transaction, we fall back to using the report year (report_year in both<br>tables) instead,  making the same cycle adjustment as necessary. If no transaction year is<br>specified, the results default to the most current cycle.<br>|
|min_date|query|string(date)|false|Minimum date|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|disbursement_purpose_category|query|[string]|false|Disbursement purpose category|
|recipient_name|query|[string]|false|Name of the entity receiving the disbursement|
|recipient_state|query|[string]|false|State of recipient|
|recipient_city|query|[string]|false|City of recipient|
|min_image_number|query|string|false|Minium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|spender_committee_org_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter code for the kind for organization:<br>        - C corporation<br>        - L labor organization<br>        - M membership organization<br>        - T trade association<br>        - V cooperative<br>        - W corporation without capital stock<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|recipient_committee_id|query|[string]|false|The FEC identifier should be represented here if the contributor is registered with the FEC.|
|min_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts greater than a value.|
|max_date|query|string(date)|false|Maximum date|

## get/schedules/schedule_b/by_purpose/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_b/by_purpose/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_b/by_purpose/`


Schedule B disbursements aggregated by disbursement purpose category. To avoid double counting,
memoed items are not included.
Purpose is a combination of transaction codes, category codes and disbursement description.
Inspect the `disbursement_purpose` sql function within the migrations for more details.


<h3 id="getschedulesschedulebbypurpose-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|purpose|query|[string]|false|Disbursement purpose category|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|

`GET /schedules/schedule_b/efile/`


Efiling endpoints provide real-time campaign finance data received from electronic filers. Efiling endpoints only contain the most recent four months of data and don't contain the processed and coded data that you can find on other endpoints.

## get/schedules/schedule_b/{sub_id}/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_b/string/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_b/{sub_id}/`


Schedule B filings describe itemized disbursements. This data
explains how committees and other filers spend their money. These figures are
reported as part of forms F3, F3X and F3P.

The data is divided in two-year periods, called `two_year_transaction_period`, which
is derived from the `report_year` submitted of the corresponding form. If no value is supplied, the results will
default to the most recent two-year period that is named after the ending,
even-numbered year.

Due to the large quantity of Schedule B filings, this endpoint is not paginated by
page number. Instead, you can request the next page of results by adding the values in
the `last_indexes` object from `pagination` to the URL of your last request. For
example, when sorting by `disbursement_date`, you might receive a page of
results with the following pagination information:

```
pagination: {
    pages: 965191,
    per_page: 20,
    count: 19303814,
    last_indexes: {
        last_index: "230906248",
        last_disbursement_date: "2014-07-04"
    }
}
```

To fetch the next page of sorted results, append `last_index=230906248` and
`last_disbursement_date=2014-07-04` to the URL.  We strongly advise paging through
these results by using the sort indices (defaults to sort by disbursement date, e.g.
`last_disbursement_date`), otherwise some resources may be unintentionally filtered out.
This resource uses keyset pagination to improve query performance
and these indices are required to properly page through this large dataset.

Note: because the Schedule B data includes many records, counts for
large result sets are approximate; you will want to page through the records until no records are returned.


<h3 id="getschedulesschedulebsubid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disbursement_description|query|[string]|false|Description of disbursement|
|max_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts less than a value.|
|max_image_number|query|string|false|Maxium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|image_number|query|[string]|false|<br>An unique identifier for each page where the electronic or paper filing is reported.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|

|line_number|query|string|false|Filter for form and line number using the following format: `FORM-LINENUMBER`.  For example an argument such as `F3X-16` would filter down to all entries from form `F3X` line number `16`.|
|spender_committee_designation|query|[string]|false|The one-letter designation code of the organization:<br>         - A authorized by a candidate<br>         - J joint fundraising committee<br>         - P principal campaign committee of a candidate<br>         - U unauthorized<br>         - B lobbyist/registrant PAC<br>         - D leadership PAC<br>|
|last_disbursement_amount|query|number(float)|false|When sorting by `disbursement_amount`, this is populated with the `disbursement_amount` of the last result.  However, you will need to pass the index of that last result to `last_index` to get the next page.|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|last_index|query|integer(int32)|false|Index of last result from previous page|
|spender_committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|two_year_transaction_period|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>This is a two-year period that is derived from the year a transaction took place in the<br>Itemized Schedule A and Schedule B tables. In cases where we have the date of the transaction<br>(contribution_receipt_date in schedules/schedule_a, disbursement_date in schedules/schedule_b)<br>the two_year_transaction_period is named after the ending, even-numbered year. If we do not<br>have the date  of the transaction, we fall back to using the report year (report_year in both<br>tables) instead,  making the same cycle adjustment as necessary. If no transaction year is<br>specified, the results default to the most current cycle.<br>|
