|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|recipient_committee_id|query|[string]|false|The FEC identifier should be represented here if the contributor is registered with the FEC.|

<h1 id="openfec-loans">loans</h1>

Schedule C shows all loans, endorsements and loan guarantees a committee receives or makes.

## get/schedules/schedule_c/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_c/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_c/`


Schedule C shows all loans, endorsements and loan guarantees a committee
receives or makes.

The committee continues to report the loan until it is repaid.

<h1 id="openfec-independent-expenditures">independent expenditures</h1>

Schedule E covers the line item expenditures for independent expenditures. For example, if a super PAC bought ads on TV to oppose a federal candidate, each ad purchase would be recorded here with the expenditure amount, name and id of the candidate, and whether the ad supported or opposed the candidate. 

 An independent expenditure is an expenditure for a communication "expressly advocating the election or defeat of a clearly identified candidate that is not made in cooperation, consultation, or concert with, or at the request or suggestion of, a candidate, a candidate’s authorized committee, or their agents, or a political party or its agents." 

 Aggregates by candidate do not include 24 and 48 hour reports. This ensures we don't double count expenditures and the totals are more accurate. You can still find the information from 24 and 48 hour reports in `/schedule/schedule_e/`.

## get/schedules/schedule_e/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_e/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_e/`


Schedule E covers the line item expenditures for independent expenditures. For example, if a super PAC
bought ads on TV to oppose a federal candidate, each ad purchase would be recorded here with
the expenditure amount, name and id of the candidate, and whether the ad supported or opposed the candidate.

An independent expenditure is an expenditure for a communication "expressly advocating the election or
defeat of a clearly identified candidate that is not made in cooperation, consultation, or concert with,
or at the request or suggestion of, a candidate, a candidate’s authorized committee, or their agents, or
a political party or its agents."

Aggregates by candidate do not include 24 and 48 hour reports. This ensures we don't double count expenditures
and the totals are more accurate. You can still find the information from 24 and 48 hour reports in
`/schedule/schedule_e/`.

Due to the large quantity of Schedule E filings, this endpoint is not paginated by
page number. Instead, you can request the next page of results by adding the values in
the `last_indexes` object from `pagination` to the URL of your last request. For
example, when sorting by `expenditure_amount`, you might receive a page of
results with the following pagination information:

```
 "pagination": {
    "count": 152623,
    "last_indexes": {
      "last_index": "3023037",
      "last_expenditure_amount": -17348.5
    },
    "per_page": 20,
    "pages": 7632
  }
}
```

To fetch the next page of sorted results, append `last_index=3023037` and
`last_expenditure_amount=` to the URL.  We strongly advise paging through
these results by using the sort indices (defaults to sort by disbursement date,
e.g. `last_disbursement_date`), otherwise some resources may be unintentionally
filtered out.  This resource uses keyset pagination to improve query performance
and these indices are required to properly page through this large dataset.

Note: because the Schedule E data includes many records, counts for
large result sets are approximate; you will want to page through the records until no records are returned.


<h3 id="getschedulesschedulee-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_dissemination_date|query|string(date)|false|Selects all items distributed by this committee before this date|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|payee_name|query|[string]|false|<br>Name of the entity that received the payment.<br>|
|q_spender|query|[string]|false|<br>Keyword search for spender name or ID<br>|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|last_index|query|integer(int32)|false|Index of last result from previous page|
|min_dissemination_date|query|string(date)|false|Selects all items distributed by this committee after this date|
|candidate_office_state|query|[string]|false|US state or territory|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|filing_form|query|[string]|false|The form where the underlying data comes from, for example, Form 1 would appear as F1:<br>    - F1   Statement of Organization<br>    - F1M  Notification of Multicandidate Status<br>    - F2   Statement of Candidacy<br>    - F3   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee<br>    - F3P  Report of Receipts and Disbursements by an Authorized Committee of a Candidate for     The Office of President or Vice President<br>    - F3L  Report of Contributions Bundled by Lobbyists/Registrants and Lobbyist/Registrant PACs<br>    - F3X  Report of Receipts and Disbursements for other than an Authorized Committee<br>    - F4   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for a Committee or Organization Supporting a Nomination Convention<br>    - F5   Report of Independent Expenditures Made and Contributions Received<br>    - F6   48 Hour Notice of Contributions/Loans Received<br>    - F7   Report of Communication Costs by Corporations and Membership Organizations<br>    - F8   Debt Settlement Plan<br>    - F9   24 Hour Notice of Disbursements for Electioneering Communications<br>    - F13  Report of Donations Accepted for Inaugural Committee<br>    - F99  Miscellaneous Text<br>    - FRQ  Request for Additional Information<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|max_amount|query|string|false|Filter for all amounts less than a value.|
|max_image_number|query|string|false|Maxium image number of the page where the schedule item is reported|
|min_filing_date|query|string(date)|false|<br>Selects all filings received after this date<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|support_oppose_indicator|query|[string]|false|Explains if the money was spent in order to support or oppose a candidate or candidates. (Coded S or O for support or oppose.) This indicator applies to independent expenditures and communication costs.|
|candidate_office|query|[string]|false|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|

|last_support_oppose_indicator|query|string|false|<br>When sorting by `support_oppose_indicator`,<br>this is populated with the `support_oppose_indicator` of the last result.<br>However, you will need to pass the index of that last result to `last_index`<br>to get the next page.'<br>|

|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|

|image_number|query|[string]|false|<br>An unique identifier for each page where the electronic or paper filing is reported.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|
|max_date|query|string(date)|false|Maximum date|


`GET /schedules/schedule_e/by_candidate/`


Schedule E receipts aggregated by recipient candidate. To avoid double
counting, memoed items are not included.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|office|query|string|false|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|

|state|query|string|false|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|support_oppose|query|string|false|Support or opposition|
|election_full|query|boolean|false|`True` indicates that full election period of a candidate.<br>`False` indicates that two year election cycle.|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|sort|query|string|false|Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order.<br>|

`GET /schedules/schedule_e/efile/`


Efiling endpoints provide real-time campaign finance data received from electronic filers. Efiling endpoints only contain the most recent four months of data and don't contain the processed and coded data that you can find on other endpoints.

<h1 id="openfec-party-coordinated-expenditures">party-coordinated expenditures</h1>

Schedule F, it shows all special expenditures a national or state party committee makes in connection with the general election campaigns of federal candidates.

## get/schedules/schedule_f/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_f/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_f/`


Schedule F, it shows all special expenditures a national or state party committee
makes in connection with the general election campaigns of federal candidates.

These coordinated party expenditures do not count against the contribution limits but are subject to other limits,
these limits are detailed in Chapter 7 of the FEC Campaign Guide for Political Party Committees.


<h3 id="getschedulesschedulef-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## get/schedules/schedule_f/{sub_id}/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/schedules/schedule_f/string/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/schedule_f/{sub_id}/`


Schedule F, it shows all special expenditures a national or state party committee
makes in connection with the general election campaigns of federal candidates.

These coordinated party expenditures do not count against the contribution limits but are subject to other limits,
these limits are detailed in Chapter 7 of the FEC Campaign Guide for Political Party Committees.

|---|---|---|---|---|

|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|sub_id|path|string|true|none|

<h1 id="openfec-communication-cost">communication cost</h1>

Reports of communication costs by corporations and membership organizations from the FEC [F7 forms](https://www.fec.gov/pdf/forms/fecform7.pdf).

## get/communication_costs/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/communication_costs/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /communication_costs/`


52 U.S.C. 30118 allows "communications by a corporation to its stockholders and executive or administrative personnel and their families or by a labor organization to its members and their families on any subject," including the express advocacy of the election or defeat of any Federal candidate.  The costs of such communications must be reported to the Federal Election Commission under certain circumstances.

|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|

|min_date|query|string(date)|false|Minimum date|

<h1 id="openfec-electioneering">electioneering</h1>

An electioneering communication is any broadcast, cable or satellite communication that fulfills each of the following conditions: 

 _The communication refers to a clearly identified federal candidate._ 

 _The communication is publicly distributed by a television station, radio station, cable television system or satellite system for a fee._ 

 _The communication is distributed within 60 days prior to a general election or 30 days prior to a primary election to federal office._

## get/electioneering/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/electioneering/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```


`GET /rad-analyst/`


Use this endpoint to look up the RAD Analyst for a committee.

The mission of the Reports Analysis Division (RAD) is to ensure that
campaigns and political committees file timely and accurate reports that fully disclose
their financial activities.  RAD is responsible for reviewing statements and financial
reports filed by political committees participating in federal elections, providing
assistance and guidance to the committees to properly file their reports, and for taking
appropriate action to ensure compliance with the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA).

|telephone_ext|query|[integer(int32)]|false|Telephone extension of RAD analyst|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|

<h1 id="openfec-audit">audit</h1>

The agency’s monitoring process may detect potential violations through a review of a committee’s reports or through a Commission audit. By law, all enforcement cases must remain confidential until they’re closed. 

 The Commission is required by law to audit Presidential campaigns that accept public funds. In addition, the Commission audits a committee when it appears not to have met the threshold requirements for substantial compliance with the Federal Election Campaign Act. The audit determines whether the committee complied with limitations, prohibitions and disclosure requirements. 

 These endpoints contain Final Audit Reports approved by the Commission since inception.

## get/audit-case/

> Code samples

```bash
curl "https://example.com/audit-case/?api_key=DEMO_KEY&api_key=${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Api-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /audit-case/`


This endpoint contains Final Audit Reports approved by the Commission since inception.
The search can be based on information about the audited committee (Name, FEC ID Number, Type, 
Election Cycle) or the issues covered in the report.


<h3 id="getaudit-case-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audit_case_id|query|[string]|false|<br>Primary/foreign key for audit tables<br>|
|cycle|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>Filter records to only those that are applicable to a given two-year<br>period. This cycle follows the traditional House election cycle and<br>subdivides the presidential and Senate elections into comparable<br>two-year blocks. The cycle begins with an odd year and is named for its<br>ending, even year.<br>|
|sub_category_id|query|string|false|<br>The finding id of an audit. Finding are a category of broader issues. Each category has an unique ID.<br>|
|sort_nulls_last|query|boolean|false|Toggle that sorts null values last|
|sort_hide_null|query|boolean|false|Hide null values on sorted column(s).|
|min_election_cycle|query|integer(int32)|false|<br>Filter records to only those that are applicable to a given two-year<br>period. This cycle follows the traditional House election cycle and<br>subdivides the presidential and Senate elections into comparable<br>two-year blocks. The cycle begins with an odd year and is named for its<br>ending, even year.<br>|
|audit_id|query|[integer(int32)]|false|<br>The audit issue. Each subcategory has an unique ID<br>|
|q|query|[string]|false|The name of the committee. If a committee changes its name,     the most recent name will be shown. Committee names are not unique. Use committee_id     for looking up records.|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of results returned per page. Defaults to 20.|
|max_election_cycle|query|integer(int32)|false|<br>Filter records to only those that are applicable to a given two-year<br>period. This cycle follows the traditional House election cycle and<br>subdivides the presidential and Senate elections into comparable<br>two-year blocks. The cycle begins with an odd year and is named for its<br>ending, even year.<br>|
|candidate_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|
|committee_type|query|[string]|false|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|qq|query|[string]|false|Name of candidate running for office|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|For paginating through results, starting at page 1|
|committee_id|query|[string]|false|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|committee_designation|query|string|false|Type of committee:<br>        - H or S - Congressional<br>        - P - Presidential<br>        - X or Y or Z - Party<br>        - N or Q - PAC<br>        - I - Independent expenditure<br>        - O - Super PAC <br>|
|primary_category_id|query|string|false|<br>Audit category ID (table PK)<br>|
|sort_null_only|query|boolean|false|Toggle that filters out all rows having sort column that is non-null|
|sort|query|[string]|false|<br>Provide a field to sort by. Use `-` for descending order. ex: `-case_no`<br>|

`GET /names/audit_candidates/`


Search for candidates or committees by name. If you're looking for information on a
particular person or group, using a name to find the `candidate_id` or `committee_id` on
this endpoint can be a helpful first step.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_key|query|string|true|<br>API key for https://api.data.gov. Get one at https://api.data.gov/signup.<br>|
|q|query|[string]|true|Name (candidate or committee) to search for|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_through|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Last year a candidate was active. This field is specific to the candidate_id so if the same person runs for another office, there may be a different record for them.|
|candidate_id|string \| null|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|
|candidate_inactive|boolean \| null|false|none| Candidates who are actively seeking office. If no value is specified, all candidates<br>are returned. When True is specified, only active candidates are returned. When False is<br>specified, only inactive candidates are returned.<br>|
|candidate_status|string \| null|false|none|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|cycles|[integer(int32)]|false|none|<br>Two-year election cycle in which a candidate runs for office.<br>Calculated from Form 2. The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year. This cycle follows<br>the traditional house election cycle and subdivides the presidential<br>and Senate elections into comparable two-year blocks. To retrieve data for<br>the entire four years of a presidential term or six years of a senatorial term,<br>you will need the `election_full` flag.<br>|
|district|string \| null|false|none|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|district_number|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|election_districts|[string]|false|none|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|election_years|[integer(int32)]|false|none|Years in which a candidate ran for office.|
|federal_funds_flag|boolean|false|none|none|
|first_file_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the candidate's first filing. This is a F2 candidate registration.|
|has_raised_funds|boolean|false|none|none|
|inactive_election_years|[integer(int32)]|false|none|inactive years|
|incumbent_challenge|string \| null|false|none|One-letter code ('I', 'C', 'O') explaining if the candidate is an incumbent, a challenger, or if the seat is open.|
|incumbent_challenge_full|string \| null|false|none|Explains if the candidate is an incumbent, a challenger, or if the seat is open.|
|last_f2_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the candidate's most recent Form 2|
|last_file_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the candidate's most recent filing|
|load_date|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Date the information was loaded into the FEC systems. This can be affected by reseting systems and other factors, refer to receipt_date for the day that the FEC received the paper or electronic document. Keep in mind that paper filings take more time to process and there can be a lag between load_date and receipt_date. This field can be helpful to identify paper records that have been processed recently.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Name of candidate running for office|
|office|string \| null|false|none|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|office_full|string \| null|false|none|Federal office candidate runs for: House, Senate or presidential|
|party|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter code for the party affiliated with a candidate or committee. For example, DEM for Democratic Party and REP for Republican Party.|
|party_full|string \| null|false|none|Party affiliated with a candidate or committee|
|principal_committees|[object]|false|none|none|
|state|string \| null|false|none|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_through|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Last year a candidate was active. This field is specific to the candidate_id so if the same person runs for another office, there may be a different record for them.|
|address_city|string \| null|false|none|City of candidate's address, as reported on their Form 2.|
|address_state|string \| null|false|none|State of candidate's address, as reported on their Form 2.|
|address_street_1|string \| null|false|none|Street of candidate's address, as reported on their Form 2.|
|address_street_2|string \| null|false|none|Additional street information of candidate's address, as reported on their Form 2.|
|address_zip|string \| null|false|none|Zip code of candidate's address, as reported on their Form 2.|
|candidate_id|string \| null|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|
|candidate_inactive|boolean \| null|false|none|True indicates that a candidate is inactive.|
|candidate_status|string \| null|false|none|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|cycles|[integer(int32)]|false|none|<br>Two-year election cycle in which a candidate runs for office.<br>Calculated from Form 2. The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year. This cycle follows<br>the traditional house election cycle and subdivides the presidential<br>and Senate elections into comparable two-year blocks. To retrieve data for<br>the entire four years of a presidential term or six years of a senatorial term,<br>you will need the `election_full` flag.<br>|
|district|string \| null|false|none|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|district_number|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|One-letter code explaining if the candidate is:<br>        - C present candidate<br>        - F future candidate<br>        - N not yet a candidate<br>        - P prior candidate<br>|
|election_districts|[string]|false|none|Two-digit US House distirict of the office the candidate is running for. Presidential, Senate and House at-large candidates will have District 00.|
|election_years|[integer(int32)]|false|none|Years in which a candidate ran for office.|
|federal_funds_flag|boolean|false|none|none|
|first_file_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the candidate's first filing. This is a F2 candidate registration.|
|flags|string \| null|false|none|none|
|has_raised_funds|boolean|false|none|none|
|incumbent_challenge|string \| null|false|none|One-letter code ('I', 'C', 'O') explaining if the candidate is an incumbent, a challenger, or if the seat is open.|
|incumbent_challenge_full|string \| null|false|none|Explains if the candidate is an incumbent, a challenger, or if the seat is open.|
|last_f2_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the candidate's most recent Form 2|
|last_file_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the candidate's most recent filing|
|load_date|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Date the information was loaded into the FEC systems. This can be affected by reseting systems and other factors, refer to receipt_date for the day that the FEC received the paper or electronic document. Keep in mind that paper filings take more time to process and there can be a lag between load_date and receipt_date. This field can be helpful to identify paper records that have been processed recently.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Name of candidate running for office|
|office|string \| null|false|none|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|office_full|string \| null|false|none|Federal office candidate runs for: House, Senate or presidential|
|party|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter code for the party affiliated with a candidate or committee. For example, DEM for Democratic Party and REP for Republican Party.|
|party_full|string \| null|false|none|Party affiliated with a candidate or committee|
|state|string \| null|false|none|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amendment_chain|[number]|false|none|<br>The first value in the chain is the original filing.  The ordering in the chain reflects the order the<br>amendments were filed up to the amendment being inspected.<br>|
|amendment_indicator|string \| null|false|none|none|
|amendment_indicator_full|string \| null|false|none|none|
|beginning_image_number|string|false|none|none|
|candidate_contribution_period|number \| null|false|none|none|
|candidate_contribution_ytd|number \| null|false|none|none|
|cash_on_hand_beginning_period|number \| null|false|none|Balance for the committee at the start of the two-year period|
|cash_on_hand_end_period|number \| null|false|none|Ending cash balance on the most recent filing|
|committee_id|string \| null|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|committee_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the committee. If a committee changes its name,     the most recent name will be shown. Committee names are not unique. Use committee_id     for looking up records.|
|committee_type|string|false|none|none|
|coverage_end_date|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Ending date of the reporting period|
|coverage_start_date|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Beginning date of the reporting period|
|csv_url|string|false|none|none|
|cycle|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Filter records to only those that are applicable to a given two-year<br>period. This cycle follows the traditional House election cycle and<br>subdivides the presidential and Senate elections into comparable<br>two-year blocks. |committee_id|string \| null|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|committee_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the committee. If a committee changes its name,     the most recent name will be shown. Committee names are not unique. Use committee_id     for looking up records.|
|coverage_end_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Ending date of the reporting period|

|filed_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Timestamp of electronic or paper record that FEC received|
|form_type|string \| null|false|none|The form where the underlying data comes from, for example, Form 1 would appear as F1:<br>    - F1   Statement of Organization<br>    - F1M  Notification of Multicandidate Status<br>    - F2   Statement of Candidacy<br>    - F3   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee<br>    - F3P  Report of Receipts and Disbursements by an Authorized Committee of a Candidate for     The Office of President or Vice President<br>    - F3L  Report of Contributions Bundled by Lobbyists/Registrants and Lobbyist/Registrant PACs<br>    - F3X  Report of Receipts and Disbursements for other than an Authorized Committee<br>    - F4   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for a Committee or Organization Supporting a Nomination Convention<br>    - F5   Report of Independent Expenditures Made and Contributions Received<br>    - F6   48 Hour Notice of Contributions/Loans Received<br>    - F7   Report of Communication Costs by Corporations and Membership Organizations<br>    - F8   Debt Settlement Plan<br>    - F9   24 Hour Notice of Disbursements for Electioneering Communications<br>    - F13  Report of Donations Accepted for Inaugural Committee<br>    - F99  Miscellaneous Text<br>    - FRQ  Request for Additional Information<br>|
|html_url|string|false|none|none|
|is_amended|boolean|false|none|none|
|load_timestamp|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Date the information was loaded into the FEC systems. This can be affected by reseting systems and other factors, refer to receipt_date for the day that the FEC received the paper or electronic document. Keep in mind that paper filings take more time to process and there can be a lag between load_date and receipt_date. This field can be helpful to identify paper records that have been processed recently.|
|most_recent|boolean|false|none|none|
|most_recent_filing|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|pdf_url|string|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additional_bank_names|[string]|false|none|<br>Additional banks or depositories in which the committee deposits funds, holds accounts, rents safety deposit boxes or maintains funds.<br>|
|amendment_chain|[number]|false|none|<br>The first value in the chain is the original filing.  The ordering in the chain reflects the order the<br>amendments were filed up to the amendment being inspected.<br>|
|amendment_indicator|string \| null|false|none|<br>The first value in the chain is the original filing.  The ordering in the chain reflects the order the<br>amendments were filed up to the amendment being inspected.<br>|
|amendment_version|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Amendment version<br>|
|bank_depository_city|string \| null|false|none|<br>City of bank or depository as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|bank_depository_name|string \| null|false|none|<br>Primary bank or depository in which the committee deposits funds, holds accounts, rents safety deposit boxes or maintains funds.<br>|
|bank_depository_state|string \| null|false|none|<br>State of bank or depository as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|bank_depository_street_1|string \| null|false|none|<br>Street of bank or depository as reported on their Form 1.<br>|
|bank_depository_street_2|string \| null|false|none|<br>Second line of the street of bank or depository as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|bank_depository_zip|string \| null|false|none|<br>Zip code of bank or depository as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|beginning_image_number|string|false|none|none|
|candidate_id|string \| null|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|
|candidate_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of candidate running for office|
|cash_on_hand_beginning_period|number \| null|false|none|Balance for the committee at the start of the two-year period|
|cash_on_hand_end_period|number \| null|false|none|Ending cash balance on the most recent filing|
|committee_id|string \| null|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|committee_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the committee. If a committee changes its name,     the most recent name will be shown. Committee names are not unique. Use committee_id     for looking up records.|
|committee_type|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|coverage_end_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Ending date of the reporting period|
|coverage_start_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Beginning date of the reporting period|
|csv_url|string|false|none|none|
|cycle|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Filter records to only those that were applicable to a given<br>two-year period.The cycle begins with an odd year and is named<br>for its ending, even year.<br>|
|debts_owed_by_committee|number \| null|false|none|Debts owed by the committee|
|debts_owed_to_committee|number \| null|false|none|Debts owed to the committee|
|document_description|string|false|none|none|
|document_type|string \| null|false|none|<br>The type of document for documents other than reports:<br>    - 2 24 Hour Contribution Notice<br>    - 4 48 Hour Contribution Notice<br>    - A Debt Settlement Statement<br>    - B Acknowledgment of Receipt of Debt Settlement Statement<br>    - C RFAI: Debt Settlement First Notice<br>    - D Commission Debt Settlement Review<br>    - E Commission Response TO Debt Settlement Request<br>    - F Administrative Termination<br>    - G Debt Settlement Plan Amendment<br>    - H Disavowal Notice<br>    - I Disavowal Response<br>    - J Conduit Report<br>    - K Termination Approval<br>    - L Repeat Non-Filer Notice<br>    - M Filing Frequency Change Notice<br>    - N Paper Amendment to Electronic Report<br>    - O Acknowledgment of Filing Frequency Change<br>    - S RFAI: Debt Settlement Second<br>    - T Miscellaneous Report TO FEC<br>    - V Repeat Violation Notice (441A OR 441B)<br>    - P Notice of Paper Filing<br>    - R F3L Filing Frequency Change Notice<br>    - Q Acknowledgment of F3L Filing Frequency Change<br>    - U Unregistered Committee Notice<br>|
|document_type_full|string \| null|false|none|<br>The type of document for documents other than reports:<br>    - 2 24 Hour Contribution Notice<br>    - 4 48 Hour Contribution Notice<br>    - A Debt Settlement Statement<br>    - B Acknowledgment of Receipt of Debt Settlement Statement<br>    - C RFAI: Debt Settlement First Notice<br>    - D Commission Debt Settlement Review<br>    - E Commission Response TO Debt Settlement Request<br>    - F Administrative Termination<br>    - G Debt Settlement Plan Amendment<br>    - H Disavowal Notice<br>    - I Disavowal Response<br>    - J Conduit Report<br>    - K Termination Approval<br>    - L Repeat Non-Filer Notice<br>    - M Filing Frequency Change Notice<br>    - N Paper Amendment to Electronic Report<br>    - O Acknowledgment of Filing Frequency Change<br>    - S RFAI: Debt Settlement Second<br>    - T Miscellaneous Report TO FEC<br>    - V Repeat Violation Notice (441A OR 441B)<br>    - P Notice of Paper Filing<br>    - R F3L Filing Frequency Change Notice<br>    - Q Acknowledgment of F3L Filing Frequency Change<br>    - U Unregistered Committee Notice<br>|
|election_year|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Year of election|
|ending_image_number|string|false|none|none|
|fec_file_id|string|false|none|none|
|fec_url|string|false|none|none|
|file_number|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Filing ID number|
|form_category|string \| null|false|none|<br>The forms filed are categorized based on the nature of the filing:<br>    - REPORT F3, F3X, F3P, F3L, F4, F5, F7, F13<br>    - NOTICE F5, F24, F6, F9, F10, F11<br>    - STATEMENT F1, F2<br>    - OTHER F1M, F8, F99, F12, FRQ<br>|
|form_type|string \| null|false|none|The form where the underlying data comes from, for example, Form 1 would appear as F1:<br>    - F1   Statement of Organization<br>    - F1M  Notification of Multicandidate Status<br>    - F2   Statement of Candidacy<br>    - F3   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee<br>    - F3P  Report of Receipts and Disbursements by an Authorized Committee of a Candidate for     The Office of President or Vice President<br>    - F3L  Report of Contributions Bundled by Lobbyists/Registrants and Lobbyist/Registrant PACs<br>    - F3X  Report of Receipts and Disbursements for other than an Authorized Committee<br>    - F4   Report of Receipts and Disbursements for a Committee or Organization Supporting a Nomination Convention<br>    - F5   Report of Independent Expenditures Made and Contributions Received<br>    - F6   48 Hour Notice of Contributions/Loans Received<br>    - F7   Report of Communication Costs by Corporations and Membership Organizations<br>    - F8   Debt Settlement Plan<br>    - F9   24 Hour Notice of Disbursements for Electioneering Communications<br>    - F13  Report of Donations Accepted for Inaugural Committee<br>    - F99  Miscellaneous Text<br>    - FRQ  Request for Additional Information<br>|
|house_personal_funds|number \| null|false|none|House personal funds|
|html_url|string \| null|false|none|<br>HTML link to the filing.<br>|
|is_amended|boolean \| null|false|none|<br>False indicates that a report is the most recent. True indicates that the report has been superseded by an amendment.<br>|
|means_filed|string \| null|false|none|The method used to file with the FEC, either electronic or on paper.|
|most_recent|boolean \| null|false|none|<br>Report is either new or is the most-recently filed amendment<br>|
|most_recent_file_number|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|none|
|net_donations|number \| null|false|none|Net donations|
|office|string \| null|false|none|Federal office candidate runs for: H, S or P|
|opposition_personal_funds|number \| null|false|none|Opposition personal funds|
|pages|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Number of pages in the document<br>|
|party|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter code for the party affiliated with a candidate or committee. For example, DEM for Democratic Party and REP for Republican Party.|
|pdf_url|string \| null|false|none|<br>pdf link to the filing<br>|
|previous_file_number|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Previous filing ID number<br>|
|primary_general_indicator|string \| null|false|none|<br>Primary general indicator<br>|
|receipt_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Date the FEC received the electronic or paper record|
|report_type|string \| null|false|none|Name of report where the underlying data comes from:<br>    - 10D Pre-Election<br>    - 10G Pre-General<br>    - 10P Pre-Primary<br>    - 10R Pre-Run-Off<br>    - 10S Pre-Special<br>    - 12C Pre-Convention<br>    - 12G Pre-General<br>    - 12P Pre-Primary<br>    - 12R Pre-Run-Off<br>    - 12S Pre-Special<br>    - 30D Post-Election<br>    - 30G Post-General<br>    - 30P Post-Primary<br>    - 30R Post-Run-Off<br>    - 30S Post-Special<br>    - 60D Post-Convention<br>    - M1  January Monthly<br>    - M10 October Monthly<br>    - M11 November Monthly<br>    - M12 December Monthly<br>    - M2  February Monthly<br>    - M3  March Monthly<br>    - M4  April Monthly<br>    - M5  May Monthly<br>    - M6  June Monthly<br>    - M7  July Monthly<br>    - M8  August Monthly<br>    - M9  September Monthly<br>    - MY  Mid-Year Report<br>    - Q1  April Quarterly<br>    - Q2  July Quarterly<br>    - Q3  October Quarterly<br>    - TER Termination Report<br>    - YE  Year-End<br>    - ADJ COMP ADJUST AMEND<br>    - CA  COMPREHENSIVE AMEND<br>    - 90S Post Inaugural Supplement<br>    - 90D Post Inaugural<br>    - 48  48 Hour Notification<br>    - 24  24 Hour Notification<br>    - M7S July Monthly/Semi-Annual<br>    - MSA Monthly Semi-Annual (MY)<br>    - MYS Monthly Year End/Semi-Annual<br>    - Q2S July Quarterly/Semi-Annual<br>    - QSA Quarterly Semi-Annual (MY)<br>    - QYS Quarterly Year End/Semi-Annual<br>    - QYE Quarterly Semi-Annual (YE)<br>    - QMS Quarterly Mid-Year/ Semi-Annual<br>    - MSY Monthly Semi-Annual (YE)<br>|
|report_type_full|string|false|none|none|
|report_year|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Forms with coverage date - <br>    year from the coverage ending date.<br>Forms without coverage date - <br>    year from the receipt date.<br>|
|request_type|string \| null|false|none|Requests for additional information (RFAIs) sent to filers. The request type is based on the type of document filed:<br>    - 1 Statement of Organization<br>    - 2 Report of Receipts and Expenditures (Form 3 and 3X)<br>    - 3 Second Notice - Reports<br>    - 4 Request for Additional Information<br>    - 5 Informational - Reports<br>    - 6 Second Notice - Statement of Organization<br>    - 7 Failure to File<br>    - 8 From Public Disclosure<br>    - 9 From Multi Candidate Status<br>|
|senate_personal_funds|number \| null|false|none|Senate personal funds|
|state|string \| null|false|none|US state or territory where a candidate runs for office|
|sub_id|string|false|none|none|
|total_communication_cost|number \| null|false|none|Total communications cost|
|total_disbursements|number \| null|false|none|Total disbursements|
|total_independent_expenditures|number \| null|false|none|Total independent expenditures|
|total_individual_contributions|number \| null|false|none|Total individual contributions|
|total_receipts|number \| null|false|none|Total receipts|
|treasurer_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the Committee's treasurer. If multiple treasurers for the committee, the most recent treasurer will be shown.|
|update_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Date the record was updated|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|committee_type|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|committee_type_full|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|count|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Number of records making up the total.|
|cycle|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>Filter records to only those that are applicable to a given two-year<br>period. This cycle follows the traditional House election cycle and<br>subdivides the presidential and Senate elections into comparable<br>two-year blocks. The cycle begins with an odd year and is named for its<br>ending, even year.<br>|
|state|string \| null|false|none|US state or territory|
|state_full|string \| null|false|none|US state or territory|
|total|number \| null|false|none|The calculated total.|

In cases where we have the date of the transaction<br>(contribution_receipt_date in schedules/schedule_a, disbursement_date in schedules/schedule_b)<br>the two_year_transaction_period is named after the ending, even-numbered year. If we do not<br>have the date  of the transaction, we fall back to using the report year (report_year in both<br>tables) instead,  making the same cycle adjustment as necessary. ### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|affiliated_committee_name|string \| null|false|none|<br>Affiliated committee or connected organization<br>|
|candidate_ids|[string]|false|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each candidate registered with the FEC.<br>If a person runs for several offices, that person will have separate candidate IDs for each office.<br>|
|cash_on_hand_end_period|number|false|none|none|
|city|string \| null|false|none|<br>City of committee as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|committee_id|string|true|none|<br>A unique identifier assigned to each committee or filer registered with the FEC. In general committee id's begin with the letter C which is followed by eight digits.<br>|
|committee_type|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|committee_type_full|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter type code of the organization:<br>        - C communication cost<br>        - D delegate<br>        - E electioneering communication<br>        - H House<br>        - I independent expenditure filer (not a committee)<br>        - N PAC - nonqualified<br>        - O independent expenditure-only (super PACs)<br>        - P presidential<br>        - Q PAC - qualified<br>        - S Senate<br>        - U single candidate independent expenditure<br>        - V PAC with non-contribution account, nonqualified<br>        - W PAC with non-contribution account, qualified<br>        - X party, nonqualified<br>        - Y party, qualified<br>        - Z national party non-federal account<br>|
|cycle|integer(int32)|true|none|<br>A two year election cycle that the committee was active- (after original registration<br>date but before expiration date in Form 1s) The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year.<br>|
|cycles|[integer(int32)]|false|none|<br>A two year election cycle that the committee was active- (after original registration<br>date but before expiration date in Form 1s) The cycle begins with<br>an odd year and is named for its ending, even year.<br>|
|cycles_has_activity|[integer(int32)]|false|none|<br>A two year election cycle that the committee was active- (after original registration<br>date but before expiration date in Form 1), and the committee has filling activity during the cycle<br>|
|cycles_has_financial|[integer(int32)]|false|none|<br>A two year election cycle that the committee was active- (after original registration<br>date but before expiration date in Form 1s), and the committee files the financial reports<br>('F3', 'F3X', 'F3P', 'F3L', 'F4', 'F5', 'F7', 'F13') during this cycle.<br>|
|debts_owed_by_committee|number|false|none|none|
|designation|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter designation code of the organization:<br>         - A authorized by a candidate<br>         - J joint fundraising committee<br>         - P principal campaign committee of a candidate<br>         - U unauthorized<br>         - B lobbyist/registrant PAC<br>         - D leadership PAC<br>|
|designation_full|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter designation code of the organization:<br>         - A authorized by a candidate<br>         - J joint fundraising committee<br>         - P principal campaign committee of a candidate<br>         - U unauthorized<br>         - B lobbyist/registrant PAC<br>         - D leadership PAC<br>|
|disbursements|number|false|none|none|
|filing_frequency|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter <br>    code of the filing frequency:<br>         - A Administratively terminated<br>         - D Debt<br>         - M Monthly filer<br>         - Q Quarterly filer<br>         - T Terminated<br>         - W Waived<br>|
|first_f1_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the committee's first Form 1|
|first_file_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the committee's first filing. This is usually a Form 1 committee registration.|
|independent_expenditures|number|false|none|none|
|is_active|boolean \| null|false|none|<br>True indicates that a committee is active.<br>|
|jfc_committee|[object]|false|none|none|
|last_cycle_has_activity|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>The latest two year election cycle that the committee has filings<br>|
|last_cycle_has_financial|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|<br>The latest two year election cycle that the committee files the financial reports<br>('F3', 'F3X', 'F3P', 'F3L', 'F4', 'F5', 'F7', 'F13').<br>|
|last_f1_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the committee's most recent Form 1|
|last_file_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The day the FEC received the committee's most recent filing|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the committee. If a committee changes its name,     the most recent name will be shown. Committee names are not unique. Use committee_id     for looking up records.|
|organization_type|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter code for the kind for organization:<br>        - C corporation<br>        - L labor organization<br>        - M membership organization<br>        - T trade association<br>        - V cooperative<br>        - W corporation without capital stock<br>|
|organization_type_full|string \| null|false|none|The one-letter code for the kind for organization:<br>        - C corporation<br>        - L labor organization<br>        - M membership organization<br>        - T trade association<br>        - V cooperative<br>        - W corporation without capital stock<br>|
|party|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter code for the party affiliated with a candidate or committee. For example, DEM for Democratic Party and REP for Republican Party.|
|party_full|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter code for the party affiliated with a candidate or committee. For example, DEM for Democratic Party and REP for Republican Party.|
|receipts|number|false|none|none|
|state|string \| null|false|none|<br>State of the committee's address as filed on the Form 1<br>|
|state_full|string \| null|false|none|<br>State of committee as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|street_1|string \| null|false|none|<br>Street address of committee as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|street_2|string \| null|false|none|<br>Second line of street address of committee as reported on the Form 1<br>|
|treasurer_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the Committee's treasurer. If multiple treasurers for the committee, the most recent treasurer will be shown.|
|zip|string \| null|false|none|<br>Zip code of committee as reported on the Form 1<br>|
